sundayRoastScope.rule: This topic is about the kitchen generally - a proper a la carte menu, chef pedigree, food-led reputation across the whole week - not specifically Sunday lunch. At collection time, exclude a venue if the ONLY real citation found for it is Sunday-roast-specific (e.g. a 'best Sunday lunches' listicle entry with no other food-led citation anywhere). None of the sources found this session are Sunday-specific in that narrow sense - Estrella Damm judges the pub as a whole across all seven days, the National Restaurant Awards' Gastropub of the Year and Michelin's selections are not meal-specific, and Time Out's and Secret London's gastropub picks are explicitly framed around the whole menu, not Sunday lunch (Time Out's own intro lists 'fish and chips, a roast, an oxtail ragu' as three of several possible reasons to visit, not the point of the list). So no exclusions were needed at this draft stage - but this needs re-checking per-venue once the actual citation text is pulled in at collection time, since a venue could still turn out to be cited ONLY for its roast within an otherwise general-sounding list.
sundayRoastScope.overlapWithLiveArticle: Checked every name found this session against the LIVE best-sunday-roast-london.md article's actual text (not just its underlying consensus data, which carries a few more names the published article dropped). The overlap is real but splits into two very different kinds, and the distinction matters more than the raw count: (1) FULL ROAST-SPECIFIC WRITE-UPS - a dedicated heading and paragraphs about that pub's actual Sunday roast: The Devonshire, The Red Lion & Sun, Canton Arms, The Baring, The Marksman, The Waterman's Arms, The Tamil Crown, The Harwood Arms, The Bull & Last, The Camberwell Arms, The Parakeet, The Drapers Arms - 12 pubs where real double-coverage risk exists, since both articles would otherwise be writing about the same kitchen's reputation. (2) TABLE-ONLY MENTIONS - named only in the article's reproduced Estrella Damm ranking table, its 'Time Out disagrees' table, or its one-line 'Also named' table, with no roast-specific opinion actually written about them: The French House, The Golden Tooth, The Clarence Tavern, The Hero (of Maida), The Anchor & Hope, The George, The Eagle, The Kerfield Arms, The Fat Badger and The Lady Mildmay - 10 more names technically 'in' the live article, but carrying zero independent Sunday-roast judgement to duplicate; citing Estrella Damm or Michelin for these in the new guide duplicates nothing. GENUINELY NEW, not appearing anywhere in the live article at all: Prince Arthur, Shaston Arms, The Victory, The Latimer, The Tamil Prince, The Plimsoll, The Cow, The Compton Arms, Prince of Peckham, De Beauvoir Arms, The Angel Oak, Grove House Tavern, The Old Nun's Head, The Bluecoats Pub, The Adam & Eve, Heathcote And Star, The Cadogan Arms, The Mayflower, Black Heart, The Prince George, Hackney Church Brewery, Plaquemine Lock, The Cleveland Arms, The Princess Royal, The Opera Tavern, Pig and Butcher, The Holland, Victoria (East Sheen), Bouchon Racine/Three Compasses - 29 names, comfortably the largest of the three groups. So the real editorial-overlap risk (group 1) is about a dozen pubs, not the whole corpus - FLAGGING AS AN OPEN QUESTION per the task instructions rather than deciding it, since those 12 are also this topic's strongest, most-cited candidates and cannot simply be dropped; the fix is more likely in how the new article FRAMES them (kitchen/week-round reputation, cross-linking to the roast guide for Sunday specifically) than in excluding them.
sundayRoastScope.differentiationInArticle: Recommend the article's evidence block and intro explicitly says this guide is about the kitchen across the whole week, with a one-line pointer to the Sunday roast guide for readers who specifically want that meal - the same cross-link pattern already used elsewhere on the site, rather than re-explaining the whole roast guide inline.
